headings.text: Best AI Email Assistants at a Glance
What is an AI Email Assistant?
Two Types of AI Email Assistants
How We Evaluate AI Email Assistants

data.text: Honestly, "AI email assistant" feels like a new category, but when I think about it, I've had some version of an email assistant for the past seven years. Not because of AI, just because of the tool I was already using. Being able to snooze an email and have it resurface exactly when I needed it, scheduling a reply to land in someone's inbox at 9am their time zone, having my inbox automatically split by type of email so I'm triaging similar conversations back to back instead of bouncing between a sales thread and a team question and a billing issue. That's all email assistance. We just didn't call it that. The tool I am referring to is Superhuman Mail.What's changed is that AI has given us two distinct versions of this category, and they're not really the same product.The first is the layer approach. You stay in Gmail or Outlook, and a tool like Fyxer sits on top of it. It applies labels to try to organize things, it drafts replies for you, and the pitch is that you don't have to majorly learn a new tool. It's the same interface you're used to, just with a little AI help. I get the appeal, especially if the idea of switching your email client feels like too much. But in practice, you're still inside Gmail, which is cluttered by design and built for billions of people, not for someone trying to get through a high-volume inbox efficiently.The second approach is replacing the email client entirely, which is what Superhuman Mail does. There's learning curve when you first switch, but what you get on the other side is a much more minimal interface, a keyboard-shortcut-driven workflow that genuinely speeds you up, and AI features that are built into the experience rather than bolted onto it.The AI features themselves, the auto-labels, the draft replies, the follow-ups, are honestly pretty comparable between the two at a surface level. Where Superhuman Mail is better is with how deeply it personalizes the drafts. Both learn your general writing style from your past emails. But Superhuman Mail goes a level deeper by adapting per recipient based on your history with that specific person. The draft it writes to my accountant reads differently than the one it writes to a new sales prospect. Fyxer learns how you write generally. Superhuman Mail learns how you write to each person.A lot of people are using AI tools like Claude or ChatGPT to help with their emails right now. And I get it, you're already paying for the subscription, so it feels like you might as well get the most out of it. But I think what's really happening is you're optimizing for the monthly bill and not for your time 😅I tried it myself. When you connect Claude to Gmail through an automation, the drafts don't land in the right thread. They show up in your Gmail drafts folder as standalone messages with no context attached. So now you're hunting through your drafts, figuring out which one corresponds to which conversation, copying it, going back to the original thread, and pasting it in. I remember thinking, what is the point of this? I might as well have just written it myself.The most common version people do manually isn't much better. You copy the email, switch tabs to Claude or ChatGPT, paste it in, get a draft, copy that, switch back to your inbox, find the thread, and paste it in. That's four context switches per email. If you're getting 40 emails a day that need replies, you're doing that routine 40 times.Gmail's Gemini integration is the smoothest version of this and it's still clunky. You click into the email, find the Gemini button, wait for it to generate, then decide whether to accept it. It's better than a separate tab but you're still being interrupted at every step.What I use instead is Superhuman Mail, and the difference is that the draft is just there when I open the email. You open your inbox, the draft is sitting there for you. Review and hit send. So if you get more than 5 emails a day, it's so worth using a dedicated tool. I would honestly say, if you value your time, just use Superhuman Mail. Yes, it costs more than keeping things in Gmail. But if it saves you 30 minutes a day, it's worth it.A few tools worth mentioning that didn't make this list: Notion Mail, Spark, and Missive have all added AI features.But their core product is still a traditional email experience with AI layered on top, which puts them in a different category. If you want to check out full email clients and want to compare all of them side by side, we cover every option in our best email clients guide. But if AI assistance is the primary thing you're optimizing for, the tools on this page are the ones actually built around that problem.
